decision.explanation: The provided evidence from pmid-23171796 explicitly supports the claim. The source text (pmid-23171796:f02) states that cells from Braf/Nf1 mutant tumors (representing the BRAF V600E and NF1 loss profile) were insensitive to PLX4720, a Vemurafenib analogue, with an IC50 > 10uM. Furthermore, biochemical studies showed that phospho-ERK was not as effectively suppressed in these compound mutant cells compared to BRAF-mutant only cells. This directly evidences resistance to BRAF inhibition (Vemurafenib) in the specified molecular profile (BRAF V600E and NF1 Loss) in the context of skin melanoma (murine model). The claim's direction (SUPPORTS), evidence type (PREDICTIVE, as it predicts response/resistance), significance (resistance), and therapies (Vemurafenib) are all consistent with the observed outcomes in the source material.

citations.quote: were sensitive to the PLX4032 analogue, PLX4720 (Fig. 4A). However, cells from Braf/Nf1 mutant tumors were insensitive to this agent (Fig. 4A, IC50>10uM). Notably, however, phospho-ERK was not as effectively suppressed in Braf/Nf1 mutant cells (Fig. 4B).
